narrative:
The model estimates your chance of failing the final year at 13%, meaning it sees a low but real risk: about one in eight students with a similar profile would fail. The remedial courses are therefore best understood as a precaution, not a certainty that you will fail.

The strongest influence on the prediction was your record of past class failures. You have none, and that was the main factor pushing toward passing. The second most important signal was your intention to pursue higher education, which also pushed toward passing and matches the profile of students who passed. The third most important factor was your father’s education level being primary school. Among students who passed, only about 13.8% had a father with primary education, so this background factor added risk toward failing.

To improve your position, treat the remedial courses as structured support rather than a label. Protect the strong signals already in your favor: keep aiming for higher education and maintain your record of no past failures. Focus on what you can control now—attend classes consistently, keep absences low, use the additional teaching, and ask your mother or guardian and teachers for help early if a subject becomes difficult.
